checks.title: Clock is close to network time
checks.remedy: Enable automatic time sync (macOS: System Settings > General > Date & Time; Linux: timedatectl set-ntp true)
checks.notes: The canonical taint source. Skew past a few minutes fails TLS handshakes, expires freshly-issued tokens, and makes 'git log' timestamps lie -- each of which looks like a different bug. Exits 3/4 rather than printing a number when it cannot measure, so numeric_lt sees non-numeric input and resolves UNKNOWN(probe_error) rather than a false 0. 300s matches the fallback in ferret/bootstrap.sh; Kerberos uses 300s and it is the most defensible round number available.

checks.title: Disk space available
checks.remedy: Free space on this volume, then re-run
checks.notes: -P forces POSIX output: without it a long device name wraps onto a second line and the column offsets move, so $4 is the wrong field. Reports the volume holding the repo, not /. 500MB is a floor for a node_modules install plus a build, not a comfortable margin.

checks.title: Inodes available
checks.remedy: Delete unused files or node_modules trees on this volume
checks.notes: Inode exhaustion is indistinguishable from a full disk to npm, while df -h shows plenty of bytes free -- which is why it is worth a separate check rather than folding into disk.free. applies_if gates it because not every filesystem reports inode usage (some network and overlay mounts do not), and N/A is the honest answer there rather than a fabricated percentage.

checks.title: CPU architecture
checks.notes: Recorded, not judged: no architecture is wrong in itself. It is here because it decides whether a prebuilt binary or a platform-specific optional dependency can run at all, and because M10 wants it as a permanent fact. An arm64 machine pulling x86_64 binaries is a real failure, but that check belongs to the layer that knows what is being installed.

checks.title: C library flavour
probe: elif ldd --version 2>&1 | grep -qi musl; then echo musl
elif ldd --version 2>&1 | grep -qi 'glibc\|gnu libc'; then echo glibc
checks.remedy: Determine the libc flavour manually: ldd --version
checks.notes: musl vs glibc decides whether a prebuilt native module runs or dies with a cryptic symbol error -- the single most common cause of 'works on my machine, not in Alpine'. macOS is N/A rather than a third value: it has no libc flavour in this sense, and inventing one would make the field mean two different things. 'unknown' falls out of one_of and resolves NO-GO with a remedy, because an unidentifiable libc on Linux is a real gap in what we can promise.
